text:
A VPN is a private tunnel between your device and another computer on the internet, and all your traffic goes through it.

Normally, websites see your real address, and your internet provider or a public Wi-Fi owner can see where you connect. With a VPN, your device scrambles your data and sends it to the VPN company's computer. That computer unscrambles it and passes it to the website. The website sees the VPN's address, not yours.

It's handy on public Wi-Fi and for hiding your location. It doesn't make you anonymous, though, because the VPN company can still see your traffic, so pick one you trust.
